edges.effect_quant: Pooled meta-analytic evidence suggest a small average effect that is directionally consistent but not dramatic.
edges.mechanism: Vegetarian patterns usually lower saturated fat intake and increase fiber, legumes, and unsaturated plant foods, which can improve insulin sensitivity and LDL-related pathways. Effects on Cardiovascular disease still depend on food quality, because refined vegetarian patterns do not behave like whole-food plant-forward diets.
edges.summary: Vegetarian diet pattern appears tied to lower risk of cardiovascular disease in general adult mainly through pooled meta-analytic evidence. The likely magnitude is modest, which is why the edge is framed conservatively rather than as a headline-level breakthrough.
edges.caveats: Dose, timing, and baseline risk still matter. Observational edges may partly reflect broader lifestyle patterning, while small trials can overstate benefit if follow-up is short.
